title: ‘You don’t want to live inside his head’: diplomats’ dilemma in the age of Trump
summary: Flood of boasts, broadsides and conspiracy theories leaves envoys sifting for the signal within the Trumpian noise How does one keep tabs on, and then interpret, a president who in a single year sent out more than 6,000 social media posts, conducted more than 433 open press events and held free-associating press conferences lasting close to two hours? The White House Stenographer’s Office calculates it has transcribed 2.4 million of Trump’s words, four times the length of Tolstoy’s epic War and Peace. Tracking Trump is not just a problem for exhausted reporters – but also exhausted diplomats, who are tasked with searching for the signal in the ceaseless Trumpian noise. Continue reading...
